metaDescription: Sablan snap bean is a bush snap bean variety. About 50 days to harvest, 8.2 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Sablan snap bean is a bush snap bean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2009 as NSIC 2009 BSnBn 01. It takes about 50 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 8.22 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Sablan snap bean takes about 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 3.2 days faster than the average of the 11 snap bean varieties with a day count, 53.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 8.22 t/ha trails the average of its group, 12.46. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

rows: Took some damage but held up
Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit snap bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 13.3 cm long. The seed coat is black.
Where and when to plant Sablan snap bean

Baguio beans like cool weather, so most come from the highlands of Benguet and Mountain Province. Pole types bear longer, and bush types fit a short cropping gap. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 50 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 8.22 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
